title: CoreWeave Revenue Jumps 168% as Results Revive AI Trade and Lift Nasdaq
excerpt: The AI cloud company's $3.66 billion quarter beat expectations, its backlog reached $132.5 billion, and its shares rose 24.7% — even as its net loss widened to $709 million.
body:
• CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, up 168% from a year earlier and ahead of the $3.55 billion analysts expected, and raised its full-year 2026 guidance to $13.0 billion to $13.3 billion.
  • The stock jumped 24.7% to $60.77 on Wednesday, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 400.31 points, or 1.60%, to 25,466.19 as AI shares rallied across the board.
  • The company's revenue backlog reached $132.5 billion at September 30, but its quarterly net loss widened to $709 million from $110 million a year earlier.
  • For investors, the next test is Nvidia's earnings on November 17.

CoreWeave's third-quarter results revived the artificial-intelligence trade on Wednesday, sending the AI cloud company's shares up 24.7% and lifting the Nasdaq Composite by 400.31 points, or 1.60%, to 25,466.19. The S&P 500 gained 98.45 points, or 1.31%, to 7,619.38, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 254.60 points, or 0.49%, to 52,486.49, according to closing data reported by JBizNews.

What CoreWeave reported

CoreWeave, which rents out computing power from advanced chips to AI developers, reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, up 168% from $1.365 billion a year earlier and ahead of the $3.55 billion analysts expected. Its per-share loss of $1.27 was narrower than expected. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to between $13.0 billion and $13.3 billion, from $12.4 billion to $13.2 billion previously, and said its revenue backlog — contracted business it expects to deliver over time — reached $132.5 billion at September 30, up 138% year over year.

"This was a breakout quarter for CoreWeave, with revenue increasing by more than $1 billion sequentially."

— Michael Intrator, CoreWeave chief executive, in the company's earnings release

The loss line moved the other way. CoreWeave posted a net loss of $709 million for the quarter, up from $110 million a year earlier, a reminder that the demand story and the debt story are the same story: the company is spending heavily to build capacity ahead of the revenue it has contracted.

Why the market cared

CoreWeave had become the test case for whether demand for AI computing can support the industry's spending. Shares had closed Tuesday nearly 65% below their 52-week high, according to Investor's Business Daily, and chip stocks had sold off the previous week on worries the build-out could slow. Wednesday's numbers answered the demand question directly, and the rally spread: Nebius rose 16.5%, and Nvidia and other AI infrastructure names gained with it, according to Decrypt's market report.

The financing question

Management used the call to address the other half of the debate. CoreWeave said it expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months, and chief executive Michael Intrator said the company would not use the unsecured debt market to fund the business, relying instead on delayed-draw term loans backed by customer contracts and on cash flow, according to Summa Money's account of the report. The company also said it is largely sold out of computing capacity through 2027.

What to watch next

The rally now has to survive the sector's biggest reporter: Nvidia is expected to publish its own results on November 17. If Nvidia confirms the same demand picture, Wednesday's move reads as a reset of the AI trade; if it disappoints, CoreWeave's backlog will be re-read as concentration rather than strength. Either way, the figures investors will check first are the ones CoreWeave just moved: contracted backlog, prepayments, and the cost of the debt that funds the build-out.
